messages:
Maria Chen: ran nsys + perfetto on prod-sim with a chat-mix workload — saw p99 jumps tied to kernel-selection fallbacks when prefix-cache misses spike
Ajay Patel: can you share the nsys command and a TL;DR of numbers? :eyes:
Maria Chen: `nsys profile -o kv_trace --trace=cuda,cublas python -m bench.run --scenario=chat_mix`
Maria Chen: baseline p50 ~46ms, p95 ~140ms, p99 before change ~325ms, after prototype ~205ms
Len Ortiz: big delta. where are the hotspots on the kernel timeline?
Maria Chen: perfetto shows attention kernels + cudaGemm fallback exploding during short miss bursts; nvtx shows many small kernel launches replacing one fused attention in large-seq cases
Maria Chen: nsys slice (ordered):
```
0.00 cudnn_conv_small
0.12 attention_fwd(seq=256)
0.18 cudaKernelGemm (fallback_fp16)
0.20 softmax
0.21 kv_cache.lookup
```
Sara Gomez: fallback_fp16 — that's the path chosen by our selector for 'small batch' heuristic, right? we prefer fp16 throughput kernels when batch estimate small
Ajay Patel: yes. selector heuristic: if recent_batch_est >= 16 -> throughput kernel else low-latency kernel. problem is estimate can be stale if KV lookup extends seq mid-exec
Len Ortiz: so a prefix-cache miss causes full prefix replay -> seq_len jumps (~48 -> ~220) but selector already picked small-batch kernel -> heavy GEMM fallback
Maria Chen: exactly. nvprof shows chained kernels instead of one fused attention when seq grows after cache miss
bench-bot: run 2026-04-04T09:13:02Z — `./perf/run --trace nsight --seed 7 --profile chat-mix`
bench-bot: baseline p99=327ms, patch-proto p99=206ms, tokens/sec +19%
Ajay Patel: what's the observed prefix cache hit/miss profile? numbers?
Maria Chen: sampled 12k requests: overall hit=87%; short windows where hit<80% correlate with p99 spikes. avg reuse length ~34 tokens. misses tied to new convs and prompt tweaks
Sara Gomez: do we have per-prefix reuse heatmaps? we log prefix-id but selector doesn't see it
Maria Chen: traces include prefix-hash but we didn't expose it to selector. microtrace: kv_cache.lookup latency 0.6ms (hit) -> 5.9ms (miss). miss path enqueues ~170 extra tokens
Ajay Patel: options: cheap sync probe to inform selector (adds latency) or two-phase selection: optimistic launch for cached case, then switch to fused kernel on miss without heavy recompile
Len Ortiz: we already have both kernels shipped; switching should be just a different launch. key is avoiding many tiny kernel launches. batching heuristic could group same-prefix requests into micro-batches
Maria Chen: I prototyped microbatching by holding requests by prefix-hash for up to 4ms or until batch size 8, then pick small-batch kernel. If KV miss expands seq, switch launch path to fused attention for remaining steps. Results below:
```
// selector pseudo
if (pending_same_prefix && wait < 4ms) use small_batch_kernel;
else if (seq_est > 128) use fused_attention_kernel;
else use low_latency_kernel;
```
bench-bot: microbatch run — `./run_bench --scenario=prefix-miss-burst --microbatch-wait=4ms`
bench-bot: results: p99 down 34%, throughput +11%, steady-state hit workload unchanged (p50 ~ same)
Sara Gomez: any GPU occupancy or SM saturation issues? microbatching might change occupancy profile
Maria Chen: occupancy improved for small batches; nvprof shows fewer kernel launches, longer fused kernels, no SM saturation increase observed in tests
Ajay Patel: safety: if selector mispredicts mid-seq, what's recovery? we must avoid duplicate token emission
Maria Chen: added idempotent token guard and preemptive correction: if mispredict detected, we cancel remaining token launches and re-run correct kernel for remaining steps — no duplicate outputs
Len Ortiz: add perfetto bookmarks and a CI perf test that simulates prefix-miss bursts and asserts p99 < 260ms for the scenario
Ajay Patel: also add metric/alert: prefix-cache-miss-rate correlated with model.p99 rise
Maria Chen: opened PR 4823 w/ code, traces, perfetto links and bench logs: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4823 (draft)
infra-bot: scheduled canary deploy to staging 2026-04-05T02:00:00Z
Sara Gomez: thanks Maria — great catch on seq growth after cache miss; that correlation was subtle
Ajay Patel: once merged, run 48h soak on staging to validate long-tail. also include selector telemetry (pre/post kernel decision + prefix-hash tag)
Maria Chen: will add CI test, selector telemetry, and a prefix-hash reuse heatmap in console. will post soak results to #eng-runtime when ready
Len Ortiz: I'll review the PR later today. thanks team
Maria Chen: thanks all — keeping an eye on canary and metrics
